title: Identification of interstellar cyanamide towards the hot molecular core G358.93─0.03 MM1
question: Can the amide-like molecule cyanamide (NH2CN) and urea (NH2CONH2) be detected towards the hot molecular core G358.93–0.03 MM1, and what are the column density, rotational temperature, fractional abundance, and formation pathways of NH2CN?

recipe.goal: Calibrate visibilities and image sub-millimeter continuum and spectral cubes
recipe.method: Calibrate raw ALMA Band 6 data with the ALMA pipeline in CASA, split target visibilities with MSTRANSFORM, image four continuum windows with TCLEAN (HOGBOM deconvolver), subtract continuum with UVCONTSUB, image spectral cubes with TCLEAN (SPECMODE = CUBE), and apply primary beam correction with IMPBCOR.
key_parameters: DECONVOLVER = HOGBOM, SPECMODE = CUBE, Perley-Butler 2017 flux scale

recipe.goal: Measure continuum flux densities and derive H2 column density and dust optical depth for MM1
recipe.method: Fit 2D Gaussian to G358.93–0.03 MM1 continuum images at four frequencies using CASA IMFIT, then calculate H2 column density and dust optical depth from the peak flux densities assuming optically thin dust emission.
assumptions: Optically thin dust emission, dust temperature T_d = 150 K, mean atomic mass per hydrogen mu_H = 1.41, dust-to-gas mass ratio Z = 0.01
Dust opacity law kappa_nu = 0.90*(nu/230 GHz)^beta cm^2 g^-1 with beta ~ 1.7 (giving kappa_nu = 0.814, 0.823, 0.835, 0.838 cm^2 g^-1), and Rayleigh-Jeans approximation 1 Jy beam^-1 = 118 K

recipe.goal: Extract MM1 spectrum, identify NH2CN lines, and fit Gaussian line profiles
recipe.method: Extract spectra from a 0.781'' circular aperture centered on G358.93–0.03 MM1, identify NH2CN rotational transitions using the CASSIS Line Analysis module and JPL spectroscopic database, and fit Gaussian profiles to measure line parameters.
key_parameters: Circular aperture diameter = 0.781'', V_LSR = –16.5 km s^-1

recipe.goal: Map spatial distribution and measure emitting region sizes of NH2CN
recipe.method: Generate integrated intensity maps of non-blended NH2CN transitions using CASA IMMOMENTS and fit 2D Gaussians with CASA IMFIT to compute deconvolved emitting region sizes.
assumptions: Deconvolved source size given by theta_S = sqrt(theta_50^2 - theta_beam^2)

recipe.goal: Estimate NH2CN rotational temperature, column density, and fractional abundance via rotational diagram analysis
recipe.method: Fit a linear rotational diagram to ln(N_u/g_u) versus E_u for four selected non-blended NH2CN transitions using the ROTATIONAL DIAGRAM module in CASSIS, and divide N(NH2CN) by N(H2) to obtain the fractional abundance.
assumptions: Observed NH2CN rotational lines are optically thin and in Local Thermodynamic Equilibrium (LTE), justified by inner core density ~2x10^7 cm^-3

recipe.goal: Compare NH2CN abundance with chemical models and search for urea (NH2CONH2)
recipe.method: Compare observed NH2CN fractional abundance against other sources and three-phase warm-up chemical models from literature, and perform LTE spectral modelling using CDMS to derive an upper limit on the urea column density and NH2CONH2/NH2CN ratio.
assumptions: LTE conditions for urea upper limit estimation

score_reason: Public archival ALMA data with a single project code and single observing date, explicit CASA version (5.4.1) and pipeline tasks, exact extraction aperture coordinates and diameter (0.781''), and standard rotational diagram equations; however, TCLEAN imaging parameters (robust weighting, cell size), UVCONTSUB line-free channels, and urea upper-limit assumptions are omitted.
rediscovery_reason: The raw ALMA data (2019.1.00768.S) are public and modest in volume, the target extraction aperture on MM1 is explicitly specified, and the main results (continuum fluxes, H2 column density, NH2CN Gaussian line fits, T_rot, and N(NH2CN)) are concrete numeric values derived via standard analytical equations.
